summary: Learn to write, govern, and monitor an AI policy with ISO/IEC 42001 and NIST AI RMF 1.0.
lede: AI policy development helps governance, compliance, legal, risk and information security professionals define how an organization approves, oversees and reviews AI use. The training develops skills in policy scoping, AI risk assessment, responsibility mapping and designing approval, vendor-review and escalation workflows. Participants also practice creating use-case and risk registers and linking policy controls to monitoring, incident reporting and periodic review.
audienceIntro: This AI policy development for organizations training is for professionals who need to turn AI usage into governed practice with clear accountability, review steps, and reporting lines.
prerequisites: Participants should have working knowledge of organizational policy processes, governance or compliance procedures, and basic AI concepts used in business settings. No coding is required, but you should be comfortable reviewing policies, risk registers, and approval workflows. Experience in legal, risk, compliance, information security, HR, procurement, or technology governance will help you apply the exercises more effectively. The course is grounded in practical policy design and operational governance, so prior exposure to AI systems, third-party technology review, or internal controls is useful.
topics: Generative AI at work & AI copilots
